features.name: Physics for loose objects
features.what: Avian becomes the one collision world: level parts and models get colliders, moving parts are kinematic, crates and barrels tumble, characters push and stand on them, blasts shove them.
chunks: Avian as the collision world: colliders for shapes and models (box, hull, convex pieces, exact for still things), still / moving / loose parts, a fixed time step with smoothing; Moves become moving bodies; the walker moves and slides through it

The walker on bevy_tnua (slopes, steps, moving platforms); a game's own character collides through Avian, and the old collision code retires (Last Ascent's mech moves when it is rebuilt as a character file)
Loose parts: mass, friction, sleeping; characters push and stand on them; impulses from blasts and the winch
features.note: Two collision worlds side by side (today's and Avian's) would need every moving part kept in step twice, so Avian replaces today's. Loose things need convex shapes (Avian builds them from the mesh); exact mesh colliders only for things that never move. avian3d 0.8 supports Bevy 0.20 and has f64 and enhanced-determinism options for big worlds and multiplayer. Part 1 (2026-11-15): avian3d 0.8 runs while playing on a fixed 60 Hz step, drawn smoothed between steps; each Solid part becomes a body (boxes as boxes; still shapes and models exact; loose ones a hull or convex pieces); a Physics setting (Still / Loose) on parts, shared by instances; Moves parts are moving bodies; the walker moves and slides through Avian and rides moving bodies; everything goes back when play stops. Test project: tests/physics. MCP: the Physics setting on add_part and change_part. Part 2 (2026-11-15): the walker is a bevy_tnua 0.33 character, a dynamic body floating 1.1 m up (it walks up steps of up to 0.45 m and slopes, and rides moving parts), grip and slippery feels (Slippery ground: slow to speed up and to stop); the old triangle collision (Play::world) is gone, and a game's own character collides through Avian (Play's doc comment). The user chose to rebuild Last Ascent's mech after Beverly is built instead of porting it now: notes for that are on The mech as a character file. Test project: tests/steps; the lift traces re-recorded for the new walker. MCP: get_play's velocity, ground and standing_on come from the walker's body. Part 3 (2026-11-16): the Physics setting is a switch (Still / Loose) with Weight (kg) and Grip under it; the walker (80 kg) shoves light loose parts and can't move heavy ones, and stands on them; resting loose parts fall asleep until touched (Avian's sleeping); Blast (an impulse outward, fading to the edge) and Pull (a winch: a force toward a point for a while) are messages for blasts and the grapple to send. Test project: tests/loose. MCP: blast and pull while testing, get_play's loose_parts (where, how far moved, asleep).

chunks: The design's parts from the SVG (cut by id, every shape, colour and coordinate kept) drawn in the editor, scaled to the window with only straight runs stretching; tabs and the Level menu (Physics, Cameras, Lighting topics); the three bottom panels and their drawers; Roboto lettering
True vector rendering: exact edges for the design's shapes and icons (no approximated fades), and no rasters anywhere in the GUI
features.note: Asked for by the user (2026-11-16), so built ahead of its place in the order. Part 1 built (2026-11-16): editor/assets/ui/editor.svg holds the user's design cut into parts by id; frame.rs reads it with usvg, tessellates each part with lyon and draws it as meshes, scaled to the window (two runs across and one down stretch, so curves, angles and the logo stay as drawn); the left drawer, inspector drawer and scene drawer slide up from below on the design's grip (drag for height). Part 2 built (2026-11-16): the user chose a small renderer of Beverly's own over a library. vector.rs draws each shape in egui's order (a paint callback); vector.wgsl covers each pixel by exactly how much of its square the shape covers, summed from the shape's own edges (a storage buffer), so curves, corners, thin strokes and holes match a browser's rendering of the SVG at any size. text.rs turns all of egui's text into vector letters at the places egui laid them out: each letter's outline (skrifa, the fonts egui was given) is tessellated once and kept on the GPU, and each frame only places it (position, size, turn, colour per letter, one draw per letter shape). egui still builds its letter atlas but nothing shows it. features.name: Brush tool
features.what: A round brush with size (a 10 cm dab to a 500 m forest), hardness (soft to hard, as in Photoshop), strength and spacing that paints onto terrain, water or any part: textures, heights or scattered props.
chunks: The brush on surfaces: the size and hardness rings drawn on the surface, Alt + right-drag to size and soften it, strokes painting material layers onto parts (soft edges blended in the shader), erase, undo

The brush as a shared tool: layers that other features fill (height on terrain, scatter sets, grass, water), size presets S / M / L / XL, strength as Add / Subtract (a little each pass) or Set (exactly this density), the rules any tool carries (slope limit, height band, keep clear of paths and water, spacing, which surfaces), Place (one item exactly) and Pick, brush presets, the MCP
features.note: Planned 2026-11-17. Round brush first; other brush types (textured tips, scatter tips, smudge) later. Stored as strokes (points, size, hardness, strength) and a seed, never as paint images: the shader blends layers from the strokes on parts and the terrain works them into its own description, so files stay small and every stroke can be undone or removed. Sizing as in Photoshop (user, 2026-11-17): [ and ] smaller / larger, Shift + [ and ] softer / harder, also Alt + right-drag; fly speed moved to Page Up / Page Down. MCP: paint_stroke (layer, points, size, hardness, strength). Shared kit (user, 2026-11-17): Place, Brush, Pen and Fill, the same keys in every tab; each tab says what they place (design.html, Brush, pen and fill). Part 2 built (2026-11-18): the brush as the shared tool. Presets S, M, L and XL (keys 1 to 4 while it is out, a choice in its panel) each remember their size, hardness, strength and how they lay. Strength lays as Add (a little more each pass, covering other materials), Subtract (takes its own material away and leaves the others) or Set (exactly its strength, however often you go over it). Rules (Where it lands) go with every stroke: Slope (the steepest surface it lands on: Flat only paints tops, Any paints walls) and Only between heights are worked out in the shader where the stroke shows, so they hold wherever the part goes; Only on (a surface tag) picks which parts it paints. features.name: Change tracking and undo as diffs
features.what: Each part notes when it changed, so the editor stops comparing the whole level every frame, and an undo step stores what changed instead of a copy of the level.
features.note: Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Today the edit commit compares the whole level with the last undo step every frame when nothing is dragged, and each step clones the whole level (300 kept). Fine now, but it grows with the level: not for the big polygon, light and logic budgets or for regions. Autosave, the runtime edits layer and the per-region files use the same change stamps. Built 2026-11-20: each collection in a level (parts, wires, curves, ranges, lighting, navigation, walker sounds, materials, sounds) is a `Tracked` value (level/track.rs) that takes a new stamp whenever it is borrowed for change and costs nothing to read, so `Level::stamps()` says at a glance whether anything may have changed; the per-frame commit and the unsaved-changes dot compare the level only when a stamp moved (nothing is compared in an idle editor, checked by the MCP check through get_project's change_stamp). An undo step is a `Delta` (level/delta.rs: the parts that changed, came, went or moved in the list, and the other things that differ, each before and after), 300 kept, applied forward for redo and back for undo, the answer to the instances question joins the step before it. Autosave and the per-region files can read the touched part ids from a step (`Delta::parts_touched`). Tests: level::delta (round trips), level::track, the editor's one-step instance change, tests/mcp/check.py.

features.name: Part hierarchy
features.what: Parts can be attached to parts: move or turn a parent and its children follow; movers carry what is on them and can turn as well as slide.
chunks: Parent links and local offsets in the level file, the scene list and the move widget
Play follows the chain: entities, colliders and movers (a Mover gets a turn as well as a slide, for spinning debris, doors and rotors)
Frame-relative walking: what stands or walks on a moving, turning parent rides it smoothly, interpolated between physics steps
features.note: Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Parts are a flat list today (movers slide only; riding a mover is a special case in the walker). Sockets, prefabs, vehicle assemblies, mounts, ships with interiors, doors on buildings and the attachments that come with a model all need parts attached to parts. Subnautica's moving interior shows the failure to avoid: a walker clipped through the floor when the interior drifted. Chunk 1 built 2026-11-20: `Part.parent` (level/hierarchy.rs). In the editor every part keeps its world position and turn, so everything that reads them is unchanged; a parent that moves or turns takes its descendants along (`Level::follow` against the level as of the last undo step, run each frame and before every commit, so a drag is followed live and the whole thing is one undo step); the file keeps a child's position and turn as offsets from its parent (format 2, written only when parts have parents; older Beverlys refuse it instead of misreading it); a parent can't be attached to its own descendants; deleting a part hands its children to its parent, and duplicating copies the part with everything attached to it. The Inspect panel has an ATTACHED TO picker, the scene list nests children under their parents, and the MCP server takes `parent` (add_part, change_part) and reports parent and children. Size is not inherited. Tests: level::hierarchy, the parents round trip through the project files, tests/mcp/check.py. Chunk 2 built 2026-11-20: a Mover has `turn` (degrees about each axis, about its own middle, eased with the slide; the kinematic body is given a turning speed as well as a sliding one); a still part attached to a moving one is part of the moving body in play (its collider is a child of the moving body's, so the walker can stand on it and it carries loose parts) and is drawn where its carrier is (script::carry, after the drawn carrier is smoothed between steps); a moving part attached to a moving part is not carried yet (it moves by its own motion: nested movers are still to do, as are spin-forever rotors). Test project tests/hierarchy (a deck that rises and turns a quarter with a crate attached, the walker standing on it). Chunk 3 built 2026-11-20: the walker standing on a moving part, or on one attached to it, is carried round with it as it turns and looks round by the same turn (a kinematic body is put at its facing each step rather than given a turning speed, so contact friction doesn't drag the walker round a second time); the drawn parts are smoothed between steps. A Mover also `spin`s (degrees a second about each axis, all the time while playing) for rotors and slowly turning debris. Test project tests/hierarchy: the walker 1.2 m from the middle of a deck that rises and turns a quarter ends exactly where the turn puts it. Still to do, as they need their own features: a moving part attached to a moving part (nested movers; a hinged door on a swinging gate), attachments on loose or vehicle bodies (assemblies, mounts), and sounds following a carried part.

features.name: Bezier pen tool
features.what: Click for corners, drag for smooth curves, close a loop on the first point; curves hug the surface under them and stay editable. Lays a strip, fills a shape, scatters along or inside it, or raises and carves.
chunks: The pen: click and drag points with Bezier handles, Alt breaks a handle, close on the first point, then move points and handles, insert and remove points; curves drawn on terrain, water and parts

What a pen shape does, with the brush’s layers: a strip along it (width, soft edges: a cobbled path), a fill inside it (feathered edge), scatter along or inside (Even: one every N metres facing along it; Scattered: a band thinning at its edges; Both sides), and height along or inside (ridges, beds, flat pads on terrain); shapes stay live, Turn into items makes placed items; the MCP
features.note: Part 1 built 2026-11-19 (the pen): P in the Level tab; click for a corner, drag for a smooth point, click the first point to close, Enter finishes; then drag points and handles, click the line to put a point on it, Alt + click a point (or Delete over it) removes it, Delete elsewhere removes the curve, click another curve to edit it, Alt while dragging breaks a handle; points snap to the grid like parts do and land on whatever surface is under the pointer. Curves live in the level file (curves: id, name, points with handle offsets, closed), one undo step per change; the code is curve.rs (the Bezier maths, tested) and editor/pen.rs. MCP: draw_shape (points as [x, y, z] or {at, handle_in, handle_out}, closed, shape to redraw, delete) and list_shapes (tests/mcp/check.py). Part 2, first slice built 2026-11-19 (stretches): each point carries how the line leaving it treats geometry, Ground (default), Over everything, Air or Fall, and the line seen is laid on what it meets (curve.rs laid, pen.rs surface; cached and relaid when the curve or any part changes): Ground takes the walkable surface (a top face, or a part tagged Ground or Water; never one tagged Paths ignore or an invisible collider) within half a metre up or two down from where it was, so it lies on a slab, passes under a prop or ceiling and bridges gaps; Over takes anything visible within 1.5 m up; Air ignores geometry; Fall leaves along its handle and ends where it lands. Ground stretches draw solid, Air and Fall dashed; a small button by the selected point switches its stretch (a new point goes on as the last one went); the Ground and Paths ignore tags are new surface tags; draw_shape points take stretch and list_shapes says it. Strips built 2026-11-19: the pen has a panel (Inspect while it is out: the curve's name, Paint a strip with a material, Width, Edge, Strength); a strip paints the laid line as brush strokes onto the part under each step of it (the part whose top face the point is on, so a prop the line passes through isn't painted and a stretch in the air paints nothing), kept in step with the curve: the strokes are the parts' own, marked with the curve (Stroke.curve), made again in place when the curve, its strip or the geometry changes and taken away with the strip or curve, in the same undo step; draw_shape takes strip {material, width, edge, strength} (null removes it) and list_shapes says it. Fills built 2026-11-19: the pen's panel has a Fill group (Fill the inside, the material it paints, Feather, Strength); a fill paints the ground inside the curve (an open curve is closed by a straight line), the paint shader working out the inside and the feathered edge from the curve's outline, so nothing is painted into an image; it goes to each part with walkable ground inside the outline (a top face within a step of the line's height, as a Ground path counts it), not to props standing on that ground or parts tagged Paths ignore, and lies under a strip on the same curve; like strips its strokes are the parts' own (Stroke.fill, with the outline in the part's own frame like a brush stroke's), made again in place when the curve, its fill or the geometry changes and in the same undo step; draw_shape takes fill {material, feather, strength} (null removes it) and list_shapes says it. Part 2 finished 2026-11-22 (build 119): a path-wide default (the panel's Path group, Lines go; a point's own stretch overrides it, its button reads e.g. 'Air · path' while it follows the path and goes round to following it again after Fall), Steepest ground (default 60°: steeper faces don't count as ground for Ground lines or fills, so a path passes over a steep ramp), Sag for a stretch in the air (the panel's In the air group for the selected point: it hangs down most in the middle, like a rope), and clicking a curve's line with the pen put away opens it in the pen. Scatter moved to its own entry; height along curves waits for terrain (user, 2026-11-19). Test project: tests/pen (a path stepping onto a slab and over a steep ramp, a filled loop, a rope between posts). MCP: draw_shape takes stretch and steepest on the curve, and a point's stretch (null: as the path) and sag; list_shapes says them. Scatter, as the user describes it (2026-11-19): bits of random, context-appropriate debris that make a level feel varied and detailed (in a nature scene tree stumps, logs, boulders, sticks, brambles), so it places items picked at random from a set the user chooses, along or inside a curve. Decided with the user 2026-11-19: a path has two modes, Ground only (default: drapes onto the ground and ignores props, scatter and other paths) and Over everything (follows any geometry it meets); the surface each point was clicked on decides which level it follows, the path stays on that level between points, ground means surfaces within a slope limit and objects below step height, gaps are bridged, Water counts as ground; where two ground paths cross, the later one wins (order keys Ctrl+[ and ], Ctrl+Shift for ends, with a list in the Inspect panel, see the order note on the brush). Refined 2026-11-19 (user: a path crosses many surfaces; tags as well as rules; scatter on the ground, deep select for manual adjustment): the mode is per stretch (stored on a point, for the segment leaving it) with a path-wide default: Ground (walkable surfaces: ground, road, steps, interior floor; the path takes the walkable surface nearest in height to the previous sample within the step height, starting from the clicked level; ceilings and invisible colliders never count), Over everything, Air (ignores geometry; Sag for a rope) and Fall (leaves along its handle and drops until it hits a surface; a faucet stream is Fall then Ground). Tags: Ground forces a part to count, Paths ignore forces it out, Water counts. Precedence: the stretch's own behaviour, tags, the path's default, the slope and step rules. Scatter sits on the surface the path is following and never on other scatter; deep select (gesture to choose: Ctrl+click or double-click in; Alt is taken by the pen and brush) picks one scatter instance to nudge, delete or detach, kept as overrides by position along the curve (they can drift if the curve is reshaped a lot; Turn into items freezes everything). Confirmed by the user 2026-11-19: ground stretches draw as a solid line and air stretches dashed, with a small button on the selected point to switch its stretch behaviour; deep select is a double-click into the shape. Planned 2026-11-17. The one curve tool: the Paths tool draws its rails, patrols and roads with it. Stored as control points and handles. MCP: draw_shape (points, handles, closed, layer, width, feather). Idea (user, 2026-11-17): terrain features drawn with the pen, such as cliffs: a wedge along the curve with strong variation, and scatter (rocks) masking its seams. Live curves plus Turn into items (user, 2026-11-17). Characters tab later: hair, cloth strips and jewellery drawn with the pen, moving with physics. Keys (2026-11-17): P is the pen in the Level tab; points can also go in the air for camera and flying paths (the Paths overlay). Review 2026-11-20 found the fill outline stored in world coordinates (it would break on a moving part or after a region or origin shift); fixed 2026-11-20: the outline is stored in the part's own frame and the shader tests inside in that frame (test: a fill stays on a part that is moved and turned). Scatter is its own entry now.

features.name: Bucket fill
features.what: Click a surface and everything matching it gets the brush's layer: the same material or texture, the same colour (with a tolerance), the same surface tag, everything inside this part, or this whole floor; Connected only stops at gaps.
features.note: Built 2026-11-22 (build 121). G puts the bucket out in the Level tab; a click on a part fills everything that counts as the same, over whole faces, with the brush's material, strength and Lays (Alt + click erases instead). Fills: Material (every face with the same material laid on it; with none laid there, the same colour), Colour (within a tolerance), Tag (every part with a surface tag, the clicked part's first unless one is chosen), Part (all of the part clicked), Floor (the walkable faces within 0.3 m of the height clicked: a storey, a yard); Connected only keeps it to parts touching the clicked one, part to part. features.name: Scatter

Chunk 1 built (2026-11-23): a pen curve has a Scatter (the pen panel's SCATTER section; MCP draw_shape scatter): Along (a band either side of the line) or Inside (a closed outline), from a set of items (a basic shape of a size and colour, a share, optionally on its side: stumps, logs and boulders to begin with, any number of your own), with Spacing, Band, Size variation, Tilt, Sink and a Seed. The level file keeps only the curves and their settings, not the items: both the editor and the game player make the items when a level opens (editor/scatter.rs `grow`; the player waits for its models, so ground that is a model counts), the same layout from the same seed; items moved by hand are not kept until Turn into items exists. Chunk 2 built (2026-11-23): Where has a third choice, Volume, a closed curve's outline as the floor of a space (Volume height) filled with items in every orientation; Falloff thins items toward the edge (Inside and Volume); Spin and Drift (the fastest turn in degrees a second and travel in metres a second) give each item its own slow way, through the part Mover, which gained a continuous Drifts setting beside Spins. Chunk 3 built (2026-11-23): Rules as the brush's (Slope, Only between heights, Only on a surface tag) decide where an item may land, and Keep clear (metres) keeps items off paths (other curves that lay a strip) and water (parts tagged Water); Turn into items (the pen panel; MCP turn_into_items) makes the items ordinary parts and the curve stops scattering, one undo step; MCP draw_shape scatter takes rules and Keep clear, describes them, and list_shapes shows them. Scatter finished (build 129). Test project: tests/scatter.

features.name: Quality tiers
features.what: Presets that choose virtual geometry, cached shadows, baked light and the global illumination tier from the card (GpuCaps) and its budget; a weaker card quietly loses shadows, detail and thinking rate first.

features.name: Runtime edits layer
features.what: Everything that changes while playing (player-built pieces, dug terrain, destroyed props, parts that moved, what a level looked like when you left) is a saved list of edits over the authored level; test mode throws it away, saves and level changes keep it.
features.note: Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Voxel and survival games save only the edited chunks over a generated or authored world. One mechanism serves the save system, test-snapshot, returning to a level, building, digging and destruction. Digging stores shapes added or taken away (small and readable), and chunked data is allowed where it is clearly better (the no-raster rule is a guideline for game data).

features.name: Cached shadows
features.what: Cached shadow maps in two layers: the shadows of what never moves are drawn once and kept, only moving things are drawn each frame on top; shadow resolution by screen size.
features.note: Design 2026-11-20 (the moving-headlight case): a moving shadowed light can't be cached, and each cached lamp a car passes would otherwise redraw the whole street, so the static layer is kept and only the car is redrawn into each lamp it passes. Lessons from Unreal's virtual shadow maps: changing a mesh's level of detail or streaming in detail does not invalidate pages by itself (do it ourselves), animated characters always count as moving, and skipping updates near the camera shows as artifacts. Headlights: a short shadow range inside a longer light range, shadows only for the nearest cars, a smaller shadow map. Costs by kind (estimates, unmeasured): unshadowed lights are cheap (hundreds); a shadowed point light draws the scene six times; the sun's cascades are a fixed cost.

features.name: Test snapshot and keep changes
features.what: Leaving test mode puts back everything that moved, broke or was used up; values tuned while testing are offered to keep.
features.note: Needed as soon as loose physics parts exist, so it comes right after physics instead of at the end. Shares one mechanism with the runtime edits layer: leaving test mode throws the layer away.

features.name: Open tags

features.note: Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Tag is a fixed list in code today (Climbable, Diggable, Water, Grind rail, Perch spot, Slippery, Ground, Paths ignore).

features.name: Texture compression and mips
features.what: Compressed texture formats, mip levels and a size cap per quality tier, made in the bake cache, so textures stay inside video memory.
features.note: Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Nothing in the roadmap covered it, and textures are the biggest user of the 8 GB reference card.

features.name: Stress level and memory meter
features.what: A dense generated level (many parts, lights, props and agents) and video memory in the performance meter.
features.note: Starts as the separate beverly-bench program (a download of its own, runs unattended at 1080p and 4K, writes a short plain-text log the user sends back: card report, polygons, lights with and without shadows, the moving-headlight case, agents on the processor, memory; no personal data). Bench built 2026-11-20 (`beverly-bench.exe`, code in editor/src/bench.rs and bench/{scenes,agents}.rs; the Windows build makes Beverly-bench-windows.zip beside the main zip): it draws into 1080p and 4K images and steps each series up (1 to 64 million triangles; 100 to 1,600 lights; 1 to 32 shadowed point lights; 1 to 8 moving shadowed headlights in a lit town of 300 lights and 600 props; 1 to 16 GB of textures; 1,000 to 1,000,000 agents on one core and on all), about four seconds a step, a series stopping when it runs under 20 fps; it writes beverly-bench-log.txt line by line (so a crash leaves what came before) with fps, worst 1%, the card's time, triangles, memory and a summary of the heaviest step that held 60 and 30 fps; --quick runs only the lightest steps. First log from the user's RTX 3050 (2026-11-20) showed the first version ran ahead of the card: frames queued up, so the frame rates were the processor's (63 million triangles read 153 fps while the card's own timer said 21 ms), memory grew to 22 GB and it crashed at 4K with 400 lights; the first scene was also wrongly stopped. Fixed the same day: each frame now waits for the card, the crowd test runs on a thread of its own after the card scenes, and a scene gets two minutes to get going. Waiting on a second log from the user's card (its results, such as 1,600 lights without shadows costing 17 ms of card time, and 8 moving shadowed headlights costing about 7.5 ms, are the first real numbers). The stress level builds from the same scene functions. Its scenes then become this level. Reference card: the user's own, 8 GB of video memory (user, 2026-11-20).

features.note: Scripted tests record today's mech before anything changes, so the port can be compared step by step. What to look for when converting it (Physics part 2, 2026-11-15): Beverly no longer hands a game's character the level's triangles (Play::world, with pieces() and offsets(), is gone), so Last Ascent's own editor and player stop building once they update past this; the user chose to rebuild the mech after Beverly is built, not to port it twice. Collision is now Avian's world while playing (physics.rs): each Solid part is a body tagged PartBody(id), still ones static, Moves ones kinematic (their LinearVelocity carries what stands on them), Loose ones dynamic, plus the ground at y = 0. The mech's own physics maps onto it: its sphere-against-triangles step becomes a body of its own (a bevy_tnua character like the walker in play.rs, or Avian's MoveAndSlide), its raycast (grapple, camera, ground) Avian's SpatialQuery::cast_ray, its ground_y (the legs' foot placement) a ray down, and riding moving parts comes free. Physics runs on the fixed 60 Hz step (single precision, Avian's Gravity 9.81 with GravityScale for heavier falls): the mech's movement moves from Update with a variable step to FixedUpdate, catching one-off keys every frame as play.rs does (Play::press), and still sets Play::feet for buttons. Its recorded runs (walk, jets, grapple) will drift with the new collision: compare them, and re-record only when the user agrees.

notes.title: Idles, barks and interaction
notes.text: Crowds look wrong when everyone plays the same idle: guides suggest 3–5 idle variations per character type and random offsets so footsteps don't sync. Fidgets (scratching, looking around) start after standing still a while. Head look-at is a cheap procedural layer, and hands reach handles with two-bone IK that blends in and out; holding is easy, the blend is the hard part.

notes.title: Driving
notes.text: Arcade handling starts simple and adds mechanics until it feels right: steering limited by speed (curbs understeer), the handbrake locks the rear wheels to start a drift, clean drifts refill boost, boost is spent on the way out. Simulation adds weight transfer and counter-steering; Beverly's vehicles start arcade with those as settings.
sources: Racing game approaches and trade-offs (Game Developer)
Need for Speed Heat handling model (EA)

notes.title: Flying
notes.text: Arcade flight keeps pitch, yaw and roll with automatic banking in turns, plus speed and lift limits. Manoeuvres become moves: aileron roll (a full roll), barrel roll (a roll with a pull, evasive), dive, loop, Immelmann (half loop and half roll: turn back, gain height), split-S (the reverse: turn back, gain speed), stall turn, boost.
sources: How to barrel roll (World of Warplanes)

notes.title: Moves and abilities
notes.text: Platformers hide forgiveness in jumping: coyote time (jump just after leaving an edge) and jump buffering. Air dashes usually reset on landing. Dodges pair a short invulnerability with a step; parries are timed blocks. Shooters add slide, wall-run and mantle; stealth adds crouch tiers, lean, cover and hiding in shadow.

notes.title: World sizes, terrain, caves
notes.text: Positions are 32-bit, so worlds past about 10 km jitter; the fix is a floating origin or camera-relative maths. Heightfields can't make overhangs; games add caves with sculpted volumes (smooth add / subtract shapes turned into meshes) or hand-made pieces, and build dungeons from modular kits, often laid out by a generator. Rooms joined by portals hide what can't be seen indoors; they don't suit open ground. Beverly's terrain is described by curves and strokes, not height images.
sources: Godot: double precision for large worlds

notes.title: Water
notes.text: Oceans layer a few Gerstner waves: stable and easy to tune. Rivers are paths with width, depth and flow speed per point; foam drifts with the flow. Waterfalls are usually custom pieces with mist and ripple rings where they land. Buoyancy samples the water height and pushes things up with drag. In Unreal, water fought with world streaming, so Beverly's water belongs to streaming regions from the start.

notes.title: Look: post-processing, styles, wind
notes.text: Bevy 0.20 already has depth of field, motion blur, bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, lens distortion, colour grading, auto exposure, SSAO, screen-space reflections, volumetric fog, a physical sky, TAA / SMAA and GPU occlusion culling, so these are mostly editor work. Cel shading bands light into 2–5 steps; outlines are cheap shells (gaps on hard edges) or precise screen edge detection (costlier, noisier); games often mix them. One wind (direction, strength, gusts) feeds foliage sway in two layers, cloth, flags, particles and sails.
sources: Vegetation that reacts to the environment

notes.title: Multiplayer
notes.text: Shooters and most online games use an authoritative server: each player's own moves show at once and are corrected when the server answers. Rollback (every machine simulates and rewinds on a wrong guess) suits two-player fighting games and needs a deterministic game. Multiplayer touches characters, physics, scripting and saving, so if it's wanted it should be decided early, even if it's built late.

notes.title: Space and level edges
notes.text: Classic space games fly like aircraft; Newtonian flight keeps momentum, and Elite layers a switchable flight assist over it so ships stay controllable. For the edge of a level, games warn and count down (“return to the combat area”), push the player back, damage them in a hazard zone or wrap them around; developers report wrapping rarely feels good in 3D and round areas beat square ones.

notes.title: Risks found in the second pass
notes.text: Bevy releases every 3–4 months and each library has to catch up before Beverly can move, so Beverly stays pinned and upgrades on purpose (about a session each time). Physics: one collision world, not two. Animation: Prism has no skeletons yet, so pose and key comes to Beverly. Multiplayer: a fixed time step from the start. Effects: one particle system, Last Ascent's, and the Plume Editor's files as the effect format. Rasters: decals, reflections, foliage and terrain paint are kept as math, strokes or captured at load.

notes.title: Lighting: newer techniques (2026-11-20)
notes.text: Bevy 0.20's Solari path tracer needs ray queries and now makes ReSTIR optional (off by default); wgpu's ray tracing is experimental with ray queries only, so vendor cluster acceleration structures (RTX Mega Geometry) aren't reachable yet. Unreal's virtual shadow maps keep static pages cached and redraw pages that moving things touch; MegaLights traces a fixed number of rays per pixel toward the important lights instead of a shadow map per light. For a no-ray-tracing tier: Unity's Surface Cache GI (shown in its Atrio demo) falls back to compute, AMD's Brixelizer GI is compute only, Lumen's software path uses cards and distance fields. Second-hand in places; primary pages were out of reach of the research session.

notes.title: Building, vehicles, riding and many genres (2026-11-20)
notes.text: Snap points (Valheim, Subnautica, KSP's attachment nodes with symmetry), live validity feedback (Valheim's support colours, Fortnite's red tiles), structure strength spreading from the ground, assemblies with joints that need to be strong, interiors that move with a body (Subnautica's Cyclops clipped the walker), control handover for vehicles and mounts (Unreal's unpossess, attach, possess; the rider-and-mount case needs two control paths), crowds with separate levels of detail for drawing, thinking and networking (Unreal's Mass), RTS orders as per-unit command queues and fog of war as a three-state grid, voxel games saving only edited chunks. Fortnite's devices (no-code placeable objects with options and events, code as the fallback) and Lyra's game features (genres as plugin bundles) are the model for modules and game packs. Most sources are guides and forums, not developer documentation.
